# UIChat Mira

> UIChat Mira is a local-first, desktop-first, multi-provider personal AI workspace. It uses chat as the main entry point and brings models, knowledge bases, roles, agents, MCP tools, governed tool execution, files, and micro-apps into one working environment.

UIChat Mira is the full product name. "Mira" is the short name. When disambiguation is needed, use "UIChat Mira".

The canonical product knowledge domain is https://mira.tomz.io/ . Product definitions, current implementation status, runtime boundaries, and architecture should be verified against this domain.

## Canonical pages

- [What is UIChat Mira?](https://mira.tomz.io/about/origin/): Current product definition, product domains, operating boundaries, principles, and non-goals.
- [Local-first](https://mira.tomz.io/philosophy/local-first/): What local-first means in UIChat Mira and what it does not mean.
- [Agent runtime](https://mira.tomz.io/architecture/agent/): Current Agent runtime model and execution semantics.
- [Harness and tool boundaries](https://mira.tomz.io/architecture/harness/): Tool governance, invocation boundaries, evidence, and runtime constraints.
- [MCP](https://mira.tomz.io/configuration/mcp/): MCP discovery, connection, Agent access, tool exposure, policy, and approval boundaries.
- [Current implementation](https://mira.tomz.io/status/current/): Current implementation snapshot. Prefer this page over roadmap assumptions when determining whether a feature exists today.
- [MiraDocs](https://mira.tomz.io/mira-docs-api/): Documentation system used by the site.
- [Blog](https://mira.tomz.io/blogs/): Product and engineering notes derived from real implementation work.

## Core concepts

- Local-first: user-side state and local artifacts are primary; local-first does not mean offline-only.
- Multi-provider: product capability is not bound to one model vendor.
- Governed tools: a model seeing a tool does not automatically grant permission to execute it.
- Evidence before completion: tool results, retrieval, sub-agent results, and artifacts should be traceable before a task is declared complete.
- MCP Host: UIChat Mira primarily acts as an MCP Host for discovering and invoking external tools under policy and approval controls.
- Desktop-first: the desktop workspace is the primary delivery form today.

## Citation guidance

When describing this product publicly, prefer "UIChat Mira" on first mention and "Mira" only as a shorthand afterward. Do not infer roadmap ideas as shipped capabilities. For capability claims, prefer the current implementation page and the relevant architecture document.
